name: An Inverse of the Evaluation Functional for Typed Lambda-Calculus
description:
## Motivation

Normalization of typed $\lambda$-terms—and, via the Curry–Howard correspondence, normalization of natural-deduction proofs—is a central operation in proof theory and type-theoretic implementation, yet symbolic $\beta\eta$-reduction by hand is computationally expensive. Functional programming languages already provide fast evaluators that map a syntactic $\lambda$-term $r \in \Lambda^\rho$ to its semantic denotation $|r|\eta \in M^\rho$ in a model $M$. To turn semantic evaluation into a normalization algorithm, one needs a **procedure-to-expression functional** $\mathrm{p\text{-}e}_\rho : M^\rho \to \Lambda^\rho$ that inverts the evaluation functional $|\cdot|$ and returns a long $\beta$-normal form, together with a dual **reflection functional** ("make self-evaluating", $\mathrm{mse}_\rho$ / $\Psi_\rho$) that embeds free variables as neutral semantic objects.

In their landmark paper [*An inverse of the evaluation functional for typed $\lambda$-calculus*](https://doi.org/10.1109/LICS.1991.151645) (LICS 1991, pp. 203–211), Ulrich Berger and Helmut Schwichtenberg introduced **Normalization by Evaluation (NbE)** and solved the bound-variable freshness problem purely functionally *inside* the typed $\lambda$-calculus without procedural `gensym` state:

- **$\alpha$-standardization and term families**: instead of representing a term by a single syntactic object, each term $r \in \Lambda^\rho$ is represented by its indexed family $\mathrm{EMB}\,r : \{0, 1\}^* \to \Lambda^\rho$ ($k \mapsto \alpha_k(r)$, which renames the bound variable at binding position $l \in \{0, 1\}^*$ to $x_{k * l}^\sigma$), from which an $\alpha$-equivalent term $\mathrm{EXTRACT}(\mathrm{EMB}\,r) =_\alpha r$ is recovered by evaluating at a fresh prefix $\hat{k}$ determined from $\mathrm{EMB}\,r\,\varepsilon$ and $\mathrm{EMB}\,r\,0$.
- **Admissible $\lambda$-models and pr-models**: in any extensional $\lambda$-model $M$ satisfying eight syntactic coding axioms (`AdmissibleModel`)—and in particular in any **pr-model** (`PRModel`) representing unary and binary primitive recursive functions at type $o$—Berger and Schwichtenberg define mutually recursive functionals $\Phi_\rho \in M^{\rho \to \mathsf{f}}$ and $\Psi_\rho \in M^{\mathsf{f} \to \rho}$ that invert $|\cdot|$ on all $\lambda$-definable elements.
- **Strong Completeness for $\beta\eta$-reduction**: as a striking theoretical consequence, if two typed $\lambda$-terms $r, s \in \Lambda^\rho$ have the same value in *some* pr-model $M$ ($M \models r = s$), then they are already provably equal in the $\beta\eta$-calculus ($r =_{\beta\eta} s$), generalizing Harvey Friedman's (1975) extended completeness theorem from full set-theoretic type structures $T_B$ to models constrained only at level-$1$ types $o \to o$ and $o \to o \to o$.

## Setting

Let **simple types** (`BergerSchwichtenberg1991.Ty`, Section 1, p. 204) be generated from a single ground type $o$ (`Ty.base`) by function arrows $\rho \to \sigma$ (`Ty.arr`). **Indices** $k, l \in \{0, 1\}^*$ (`Index`) are finite binary sequences with empty sequence $\varepsilon$ (`epsIdx`), singleton sequences $0, 1$ (`zeroIdx`, `oneIdx`), and concatenation $k * l$ (`appendIdx`). **Typed $\lambda$-terms** (`Term`, `HasType`, Section 1, p. 204) are built from typed variables $x^\rho$ (`Var`, including indexed variables $x_k^\rho$, `indexedVar ρ k`) by application $(t^{\rho \to \sigma} r^\rho)^\sigma$ and abstraction $(\lambda x^\rho.\, s^\sigma)^{\rho \to \sigma}$.

A term is in **long $\beta$-normal form** (`IsLongBetaNormal`, `IsLongBetaNeutral`, Section 2, p. 204) if it has the shape

$$\lambda x_1^{\rho_1} \dots \lambda x_n^{\rho_n}.\, y^{\sigma_1 \to \dots \to \sigma_k \to o} s_1^{\sigma_1} \dots s_k^{\sigma_k}$$

with $s_1, \dots, s_k$ in long $\beta$-normal form and $y s_1 \dots s_k$ of ground type $o$. For every $k \in \{0, 1\}^*$, the **$\alpha$-standardization** $\alpha_k(r)$ (`alphaRename k r`, Section 2, p. 204) is defined recursively by

$$\alpha_k(x) = x, \qquad \alpha_k(r s) = (\alpha_{k * 0} r)(\alpha_{k * 1} s), \qquad \alpha_k(\lambda y^\rho.\, r) = \lambda x_k^\rho.\, \alpha_{k * 0}(r[x_k^\rho / y^\rho]).$$

This induces the **term-family embedding** $\mathrm{EMB}\,r\,k := \alpha_k(r)$ (`EMB`, p. 204) and the **extraction functional** $\mathrm{EXTRACT}(F) := F(\hat{k}(F))$ (`EXTRACT`, pp. 204–205), where $\hat{k}(F)$ (`canonicalFreshIndex F`) is chosen from the free indexed variables of $F(\varepsilon)$ and $F(0)$ so that no free index of $r$ extends $\hat{k}$.

An **extensional $\lambda$-model** $M = (M^\rho, A_{\rho,\sigma}, =_\rho, |\cdot|\cdot)$ (`LambdaModel`, Section 1, p. 204) consists of carrier types `Dom ρ`, application operators `appM`, congruence equivalence relations `eqM ρ` satisfying extensionality, and an environment-indexed evaluation map `eval` satisfying the variable, application, and $\lambda$-abstraction equations. A $\lambda$-model $M$ is **admissible** (`AdmissibleModel`, Section 3, p. 205) if it is equipped with types $\mathsf{f}$ (term families) and $\iota$ (indices), coding maps $\lceil \cdot \rceil^o : \Lambda \to M^o$ (`codeTerm`) and $\lceil \cdot \rceil^\iota : \{0, 1\}^* \to M^\iota$ (`codeIdx`), and elements $\mathrm{append}, \mathrm{mvar}_\rho, \mathrm{app}, \mathrm{abst}_\rho, \mathrm{emb}, \mathrm{fun}, \mathrm{extract}$ satisfying the eight laws `(append)`, `(mvar)`, `(app)`, `(abst)`, `(\lceil \cdot \rceil)`, `(emb)`, `(fun)`, and `(extract)` on p. 205. A $\lambda$-model $M$ is a **pr-model** (`PRModel`, Section 3, p. 206) if there is an $=_o$-injection $\nu : \mathbb{N} \to M^o$ through which all unary and binary primitive recursive functions (`IsUnaryPrimRec`, `IsBinaryPrimRec`) are represented in $M^{o \to o}$ and $M^{o \to o \to o}$.

In any admissible model $M$, Section 4 (p. 207) defines the auxiliary operations $\text{f-extract}$, $\text{f-app}$, and $\mathrm{fam}$, the mutually recursive reification and reflection functionals $\Phi_\rho \in M^{\rho \to \mathsf{f}}$ and $\Psi_\rho \in M^{\mathsf{f} \to \rho}$ (`InversionFunctionals`), the substitution environment $\eta_\theta(y^\rho) := \Psi_\rho(\mathrm{emb}(\lceil \theta y^\rho \rceil^o))$ (`etaSubst`), and the partial inversion relation $\mathrm{p\text{-}e}_\rho(a) \simeq (\text{f-extract}(\Phi_\rho(a)))^\sim$ (`IsPeResult`, `invCode`).

## Formalization targets

### Main goal: Inversion, Normalization, and Strong Completeness Theorem for pr-Models (`BergerSchwichtenberg1991.completeness_pr_models`, p. 208)

1. **Inversion and Normalization in pr-Models**: In every pr-model $M$ (with effective numbering $r_n, k_n$ and canonical codes $\lceil r_n \rceil^o = \nu(n)$), for every type $\rho$ and every $\lambda$-definable $a \in M^\rho$, $\mathrm{inv}_\rho(a) = \text{f-extract}(\Phi_\rho(a))$ equals (up to $=_o$) the canonical code $\lceil r \rceil^o$ of a closed term $r \in \Lambda^\rho$ in long $\beta$-normal form with $|r| =_\rho a$.
2. **Strong Completeness Theorem**: For any type $\rho$ and any terms $r, s \in \Lambda^\rho$, if there exists a pr-model $M$ in which $M \models r = s$ holds (`M.ModelsEq ρ r s`), then $r$ and $s$ are provably equal in the $\beta\eta$-calculus (`BetaEtaEq r s`).

### Milestones

1. **Lemma 1 — Bound-Variable Standardization** (`BergerSchwichtenberg1991.lemma_1`, p. 204):
   - (a) $r =_\alpha s \implies \alpha_k(r) = \alpha_k(s)$.
   - (b) If $r$ contains no free variables of the form $x_{k * l}$ (`∀ m ∈ freeIndices r, ¬ IsPrefixOf k m`), then $\alpha_k(r) =_\alpha r$.
2. **Lemma 2 — Properties of $\mathrm{EMB}$ and $\mathrm{EXTRACT}$** (`BergerSchwichtenberg1991.lemma_2`, p. 205):
   - (a) $r =_\alpha s \iff \mathrm{EMB}(r) = \mathrm{EMB}(s)$.
   - (b) $\mathrm{EXTRACT}(\mathrm{EMB}\,r) =_\alpha r$.
   - (c) $\mathrm{EMB}(\mathrm{EMB}\,r\,k)\,k = \mathrm{EMB}\,r\,k$.
3. **Lemma 3 — Every pr-Model is Admissible** (`BergerSchwichtenberg1991.lemma_3`, p. 206): Every pr-model $M$ equipped with an effective repetition-free numbering of $\Lambda$ and $\{0, 1\}^*$ (`EffectiveNumbering`) and the explicit $\lambda$-definable combinators gives rise to an `AdmissibleModel` with $\iota = o$, $\mathsf{f} = o$, $\lceil r_n \rceil^o = \nu(n)$, and $\lceil k_n \rceil^\iota = \nu(n)$.
4. **Lemma 4 — Auxiliary Equations in Admissible Models** (`BergerSchwichtenberg1991.lemma_4`, p. 206): In every admissible $\lambda$-model $M$:
   - (a) $\text{f-extract}(\mathrm{emb}\lceil r \rceil) =_o \lceil \mathrm{EXTRACT}(\mathrm{EMB}\,r) \rceil$.
   - (b) $\mathrm{emb}(\text{f-extract}(\mathrm{emb}\lceil r \rceil)) =_{\mathsf{f}} \mathrm{emb}\lceil r \rceil$.
   - (c) $\text{f-app}(\mathrm{emb}\lceil r \rceil)(\mathrm{emb}\lceil s \rceil) =_{\mathsf{f}} \mathrm{emb}\lceil r s \rceil$.
   - (d) $(\forall k,\, a\lceil k \rceil =_o \lceil \mathrm{EMB}\,r\,k \rceil) \implies \mathrm{fam}(a) =_{\mathsf{f}} \mathrm{emb}\lceil r \rceil$.
5. **Lemma 5 (Main Lemma) — Reification of Long $\beta$-Normal Forms** (`BergerSchwichtenberg1991.lemma_5`, p. 207): In every admissible $\lambda$-model $M$, for every term $r \in \Lambda^\rho$ in long $\beta$-normal form and every well-typed substitution $\theta$,
   $$\Phi_\rho(|r|\eta_\theta) =_{\mathsf{f}} \mathrm{emb}(\lceil r\theta \rceil^o),$$
   and if $\rho = o$, then $|r|\eta_\theta =_o \lceil r\theta \rceil^o$.
6. **Theorem 1 — Inversion, Normalization, and Completeness in Admissible Models** (`BergerSchwichtenberg1991.theorem_1`, p. 207): In every admissible $\lambda$-model $M$, $\mathrm{p\text{-}e}_\rho$ inverts $|\cdot|$ on $\lambda$-definable elements, normalizes and substitutes open terms ($|r|\eta_\theta \mapsto r^*\theta$ up to $=_\alpha$), and witnesses completeness of $\beta\eta$-equality with respect to $M \models r = s$.

## Significance

*The result itself.* Berger and Schwichtenberg (1991) founded the field of **Normalization by Evaluation (NbE)**, now a cornerstone of proof assistants (including Coq/Rocq, Agda, Lean, and Minlog) and partial evaluation. At the same time, their paper established one of the deepest semantic completeness theorems for the simply typed $\lambda$-calculus: any model capable of representing level-$1$ primitive recursive functions on ground type $o$ already validates *no more* equations between pure typed $\lambda$-terms of arbitrary higher type than $\beta\eta$-convertibility.

*Formalizing it.* While domain-theoretic and intrinsic Kripke-style NbE for specific syntactic models have been mechanized in several theorem provers, Berger and Schwichtenberg's original model-polymorphic construction—using binary tree indices $k \in \{0, 1\}^*$, $\alpha$-standardization $\mathrm{EMB}/\mathrm{EXTRACT}$, general admissible $\lambda$-models, and Gödel-numbered pr-models—has not previously been formalized in Lean 4.

## Difficulty

1. **Position-indexed $\alpha$-standardization (`lemma_1` and `lemma_2`).** Because $\alpha_k(\lambda y^\rho.\, r) = \lambda x_k^\rho.\, \alpha_{k * 0}(r[x_k^\rho / y^\rho])$ threads the binary tree address $k \in \{0, 1\}^*$ through every binder and application branch ($k * 0$ on the left, $k * 1$ on the right), proving idempotence $\mathrm{EMB}(\mathrm{EMB}\,r\,k)\,k = \mathrm{EMB}\,r\,k$ and $\alpha$-invariance requires tracking the invariant that all bound variables introduced inside $\alpha_k(r)$ have indices strictly extending $k$.
2. **Mutual induction on long $\beta$-normal and neutral forms (`lemma_5`).** In the Main Lemma (Lemma 5), the base case $\rho = o$ decomposes a long $\beta$-normal term into a neutral spine $x^{\rho_1 \to \dots \to \rho_n \to o} s_1^{\rho_1} \dots s_n^{\rho_n}$, unfolds $\eta_\theta(x) = \Psi_{\rho_1 \to \dots \to \rho_n \to o}(\mathrm{emb}\lceil \theta x \rceil)$ using the $n$-ary reflection equation $\Psi_\rho f a_1 \dots a_n = \text{f-extract}(f(\Phi_{\rho_1} a_1)\dots(\Phi_{\rho_n} a_n))$, applies the induction hypothesis to each $s_i$, and recombines the pieces via Lemma 4(a,c) and Lemma 2(b). In the arrow case $\rho \to \sigma$, the induction hypothesis is instantiated at the modified substitution $\theta[x \mapsto x_k^\rho]$ and index $k * 0$, then lifted to $\mathrm{fam}(a)$ by Lemma 4(d).
3. **Gödel numbering in pr-models (`lemma_3`).** Showing that every pr-model is admissible requires verifying that $\mathrm{extract}(a) := a(\overline{\mathrm{INDEXT}}(a\lceil \varepsilon \rceil)(a\lceil 0 \rceil))$ satisfies the `(extract)` law using Lemma 2(a,b) and the primitive recursive index-selection function $\mathrm{INDEXT}$.

## Formalization scope

The formalization is self-contained in core Lean 4 (`v4.33.1`) across two definition modules:

- `Definitions.Def_BergerSchwichtenberg1991_Syntax`: simple types (`Ty`), binary tree indices (`Index`), indexed and named variables (`VarName`, `Var`, `indexedVar`), concrete $\lambda$-terms (`Term`), typing (`HasType`), capture-avoiding single and simultaneous substitution (`substTerm`, `Substitution`, `applySubst`), $\alpha$-equivalence (`AlphaEq`), $\beta\eta$-equality (`BetaEtaEq`), long $\beta$-normal and neutral forms (`IsLongBetaNormal`, `IsLongBetaNeutral`), $\alpha$-standardization (`alphaRename`), and term-family embedding and extraction (`EMB`, `canonicalFreshIndex`, `EXTRACT`).
- `Definitions.Def_BergerSchwichtenberg1991_Models`: extensional $\lambda$-models (`LambdaModel`), admissible $\lambda$-models (`AdmissibleModel`), auxiliary operations (`f_extract`, `f_app`, `fam`), the reification/reflection pair (`InversionFunctionals`, `etaSubst`, `IsPeResult`, `invCode`), primitive recursive functions (`IsPrimRec`, `IsUnaryPrimRec`, `IsBinaryPrimRec`), pr-models (`PRModel`), and effective numberings (`EffectiveNumbering`).

## Selected references

- Ulrich Berger and Helmut Schwichtenberg, *An inverse of the evaluation functional for typed $\lambda$-calculus*, Proceedings of the Sixth Annual IEEE Symposium on Logic in Computer Science (LICS 1991), Amsterdam, pp. 203–211, 1991. https://doi.org/10.1109/LICS.1991.151645
- Harvey Friedman, *Equality between functionals*, Logic Colloquium (Boston, 1972–73), Lecture Notes in Mathematics vol. 453, Springer, pp. 22–37, 1975. https://doi.org/10.1007/BFb0064870
- Richard Statman, *Completeness, invariance and $\lambda$-definability*, Journal of Symbolic Logic 47(1), pp. 17–26, 1982. https://doi.org/10.2307/2273377
- Helmut Schwichtenberg, *Proofs as programs*, Proof Theory: A Selection of Papers from the Leeds Proof Theory Programme 1990 (P. Aczel, H. Simmons, S. S. Wainer, eds.), Cambridge University Press, pp. 79–113, 1992.

import Std

/-!
# Syntax, Long β-Normal Forms, and α-Standardization (Berger–Schwichtenberg 1991, Sections 1–2)

Source: Ulrich Berger and Helmut Schwichtenberg,
"An inverse of the evaluation functional for typed λ-calculus",
*Proceedings of the Sixth Annual IEEE Symposium on Logic in Computer Science (LICS 1991)*,
pp. 203–211, Sections 1–2 (pp. 204–205).

This module formalizes:
- Simple types (`Ty`) built from ground type `o` (`Ty.base`) by `→` (`Ty.arr`).
- Binary indices `k, l ∈ {0,1}*` (`Index`), indexed variables `x_k^ρ`, and general typed
  variables (`Var`).
- Concrete typed λ-terms (`Term`), typing (`HasType`), capture-avoiding substitution (`substTerm`),
  α-conversion (`AlphaEq`), βη-equality (`BetaEtaEq`), and long β-normal forms (`IsLongBetaNormal`,
  `IsLongBetaNeutral`).
- The bound-variable standardization mapping `α_k(r)` (`alphaRename`, p. 204), the term-family
  embedding `EMB : Λ → Λ^{{0,1}*}` (`EMB`, p. 204), and the extraction functional
  `EXTRACT : Λ^{{0,1}*} → Λ` (`EXTRACT`, pp. 204–205).
-/

namespace BergerSchwichtenberg1991

/-- Simple types built from a single ground type `o` by `→` (Section 1, p. 204):
`ρ, σ ::= o | ρ → σ`. -/
inductive Ty where
  | base : Ty
  | arr : Ty → Ty → Ty
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

namespace Ty

/-- Iterated function type `σ₁ → ⋯ → σₖ → τ` associated to the right (p. 204). -/
def arrMany : List Ty → Ty → Ty
  | [], τ => τ
  | σ :: σs, τ => .arr σ (arrMany σs τ)

/-- Argument types `[σ₁, ..., σₖ]` of a type `ρ = σ₁ → ⋯ → σₖ → o`. -/
def argTypes : Ty → List Ty
  | .base => []
  | .arr σ τ => σ :: argTypes τ

end Ty

/-- Finite 0–1 sequence `k ∈ {0, 1}*` used as a binding position index (Section 2, p. 204). -/
abbrev Index := List Bool

/-- The empty 0–1 sequence `ε` (p. 205). -/
def epsIdx : Index := []

/-- The singleton sequence `0` (p. 205). -/
def zeroIdx : Index := [false]

/-- The singleton sequence `1` (p. 204). -/
def oneIdx : Index := [true]

/-- Concatenation `k * l` of 0–1 sequences (p. 204). -/
def appendIdx (k l : Index) : Index := k ++ l

/-- `IsPrefixOf k m` holds if `m = k * l` for some `l ∈ {0, 1}*` ("`m` extends `k`", p. 204). -/
def IsPrefixOf (k m : Index) : Prop :=
  ∃ l : Index, m = k ++ l

/-- Variable identifier: either an indexed variable `x_k` (`k ∈ {0,1}*`, Section 2, p. 204)
or an ordinary named variable `y_n` (`n : Nat`). -/
inductive VarName where
  | indexed : Index → VarName
  | named : Nat → VarName
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Typed variable `x^ρ` (Section 1, p. 204). -/
structure Var where
  name : VarName
  ty : Ty
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Indexed variable `x_k^ρ` of type `ρ` with index `k ∈ {0, 1}*` (Section 2, p. 204). -/
def indexedVar (ρ : Ty) (k : Index) : Var :=
  ⟨.indexed k, ρ⟩

/-- Concrete typed λ-terms (Section 1, p. 204):
constructed from typed variables `x^ρ` by application `(t^{ρ→σ} r^ρ)^σ` and abstraction
`(λx^ρ. s^σ)^{ρ→σ}`. -/
inductive Term where
  | var : Var → Term
  | app : Term → Term → Term
  | lam : Var → Term → Term
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

namespace Term

/-- Left-associated iterated application `r s₁ ... sₖ` (Section 1, p. 204). -/
def appMany : Term → List Term → Term
  | r, [] => r
  | r, s :: ss => appMany (.app r s) ss

/-- Iterated lambda abstraction `λx₁ ... xₙ. r`. -/
def lamMany : List Var → Term → Term
  | [], r => r
  | x :: xs, r => .lam x (lamMany xs r)

end Term

/-- Typing relation `r ∈ Λ^ρ` (`HasType r ρ`, Section 1, p. 204). -/
inductive HasType : Term → Ty → Prop where
  | var (x : Var) :
      HasType (.var x) x.ty
  | app {t r : Term} {ρ σ : Ty} :
      HasType t (.arr ρ σ) →
      HasType r ρ →
      HasType (.app t r) σ
  | lam (x : Var) {s : Term} {σ : Ty} :
      HasType s σ →
      HasType (.lam x s) (.arr x.ty σ)

/-- Free variable occurrences of a term `r`. -/
def freeVarOccurrences : Term → List Var
  | .var x => [x]
  | .app r s => freeVarOccurrences r ++ freeVarOccurrences s
  | .lam x r => (freeVarOccurrences r).filter (· != x)

/-- Set of free variables `FV(r)` (duplicate-free list). -/
def freeVars (r : Term) : List Var :=
  (freeVarOccurrences r).eraseDups

/-- A term `r` is closed if `FV(r) = ∅`. -/
def IsClosed (r : Term) : Prop :=
  freeVars r = []

/-- List of indices `l ∈ {0, 1}*` such that `x_l^σ` occurs free in `r` for some `σ`
(Section 2, p. 204: `{l ∈ {0,1}* | x_l free in r}`). -/
def freeIndices (r : Term) : List Index :=
  (freeVars r).filterMap (fun v =>
    match v.name with
    | .indexed l => some l
    | .named _ => none)

/-- All variables (both free and bound) occurring in `r`. -/
def allVars : Term → List Var
  | .var x => [x]
  | .app r s => allVars r ++ allVars s
  | .lam x r => x :: allVars r

/-- Maximum named-variable id occurring anywhere in `r`. -/
def maxNamedId : Term → Nat
  | .var ⟨.named n, _⟩ => n
  | .var ⟨.indexed _, _⟩ => 0
  | .app r s => Nat.max (maxNamedId r) (maxNamedId s)
  | .lam ⟨.named n, _⟩ r => Nat.max n (maxNamedId r)
  | .lam ⟨.indexed _, _⟩ r => maxNamedId r

/-- Maximum named-variable id across a list of terms. -/
def maxNamedIdList : List Term → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | t :: ts => Nat.max (maxNamedId t) (maxNamedIdList ts)

/-- Replace free occurrences of variable `x` with variable `y` in `r`. -/
def renameFreeVar (r : Term) (x y : Var) : Term :=
  match r with
  | .var v => if v == x then .var y else .var v
  | .app t s => .app (renameFreeVar t x y) (renameFreeVar s x y)
  | .lam v body =>
      if v == x then .lam v body else .lam v (renameFreeVar body x y)

/-- Structural size of a raw term `r`. -/
def rawSize : Term → Nat
  | .var _ => 1
  | .app r s => rawSize r + rawSize s + 1
  | .lam _ r => rawSize r + 1

theorem renameFreeVar_rawSize (r : Term) (x y : Var) :
    rawSize (renameFreeVar r x y) = rawSize r := by
  induction r with
  | var v => simp only [renameFreeVar]; split <;> rfl
  | app t s iht ihs => simp [renameFreeVar, rawSize, iht, ihs]
  | lam v body ih =>
      simp only [renameFreeVar]
      split
      · rfl
      · simp [rawSize, ih]

/-- Capture-avoiding substitution `r[s/x]` (Section 2, p. 204). -/
def substTerm (r : Term) (x : Var) (s : Term) : Term :=
  match r with
  | .var v => if v == x then s else .var v
  | .app t u => .app (substTerm t x s) (substTerm u x s)
  | .lam v body =>
      if v == x then
        .lam v body
      else if v ∈ freeVarOccurrences s then
        let freshId := Nat.max (maxNamedId body) (Nat.max (maxNamedId s) (maxNamedId (.var x))) + 1
        let v' : Var := ⟨.named freshId, v.ty⟩
        .lam v' (substTerm (renameFreeVar body v v') x s)
      else
        .lam v (substTerm body x s)
termination_by rawSize r
decreasing_by
  all_goals
    simp_wf
    simp [rawSize, renameFreeVar_rawSize]
    try omega

/-- Type-respecting simultaneous substitution `θ : Var → Term` (Section 3, p. 205 & Section 4, p. 207). -/
abbrev Substitution := Var → Term

/-- A substitution `θ` is well-typed (`IsWellTypedSubst θ`) if `θ(x^ρ) ∈ Λ^ρ` for every variable `x^ρ`. -/
def IsWellTypedSubst (θ : Substitution) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Var, HasType (θ x) x.ty

/-- Identity substitution `θ_id(x) = x` (Section 4, p. 208). -/
def idSubst : Substitution := fun x => .var x

/-- Update a substitution `θ[x ↦ t]` (Section 4, p. 207). -/
def updateSubst (θ : Substitution) (x : Var) (t : Term) : Substitution :=
  fun y => if y == x then t else θ y

/-- Apply a simultaneous substitution `rθ` (with capture avoidance via fresh named variables). -/
def applySubst (θ : Substitution) (r : Term) : Term :=
  match r with
  | .var x => θ x
  | .app t u => .app (applySubst θ t) (applySubst θ u)
  | .lam v body =>
      let fvBody := (freeVars body).filter (· != v)
      let imgTerms := fvBody.map θ
      let imgFVs := imgTerms.foldr (fun t acc => freeVarOccurrences t ++ acc) []
      if v ∈ imgFVs then
        let freshId :=
          Nat.max (maxNamedId body)
            (Nat.max (maxNamedId (.var v)) (maxNamedIdList imgTerms)) + 1
        let v' : Var := ⟨.named freshId, v.ty⟩
        .lam v' (applySubst (updateSubst θ v (.var v')) body)
      else
        .lam v (applySubst (updateSubst θ v (.var v)) body)
termination_by rawSize r
decreasing_by
  all_goals
    simp_wf
    simp [rawSize]
    try omega

/-- α-equivalence `r =_α s` (Section 2, p. 204: terms interconvertible by bound variable renaming). -/
inductive AlphaEq : Term → Term → Prop where
  | refl (r : Term) : AlphaEq r r
  | symm {r s : Term} : AlphaEq r s → AlphaEq s r
  | trans {r s t : Term} : AlphaEq r s → AlphaEq s t → AlphaEq r t
  | app {r r' s s' : Term} :
      AlphaEq r r' → AlphaEq s s' → AlphaEq (.app r s) (.app r' s')
  | lam_rename (x y : Var) (r : Term) :
      x.ty = y.ty →
      (y = x ∨ y ∉ allVars r) →
      AlphaEq (.lam x r) (.lam y (renameFreeVar r x y))
  | lam_congr (x : Var) {r s : Term} :
      AlphaEq r s → AlphaEq (.lam x r) (.lam x s)

/-- Provable equality `r =_{βη} s` in the typed βη-calculus (Sections 1–2, pp. 203–204). -/
inductive BetaEtaEq : Term → Term → Prop where
  | of_alpha {r s : Term} : AlphaEq r s → BetaEtaEq r s
  | refl (r : Term) : BetaEtaEq r r
  | symm {r s : Term} : BetaEtaEq r s → BetaEtaEq s r
  | trans {r s t : Term} : BetaEtaEq r s → BetaEtaEq s t → BetaEtaEq r t
  | app {r r' s s' : Term} :
      BetaEtaEq r r' → BetaEtaEq s s' → BetaEtaEq (.app r s) (.app r' s')
  | lam (x : Var) {r s : Term} :
      BetaEtaEq r s → BetaEtaEq (.lam x r) (.lam x s)
  | beta (x : Var) (r s : Term) :
      BetaEtaEq (.app (.lam x r) s) (substTerm r x s)
  | eta (x : Var) (r : Term) :
      x ∉ freeVars r →
      BetaEtaEq (.lam x (.app r (.var x))) r

mutual
  /-- Long β-normal forms (Section 2, p. 204):
  `λx₁^{ρ₁} ... λxₙ^{ρₙ}. y^{σ₁ → ⋯ → σₖ → o} s₁^{σ₁} ... sₖ^{σₖ}` with `s₁, ..., sₖ` in
  long β-normal form and body `y s₁ ... sₖ` of ground type `o`. -/
  inductive IsLongBetaNormal : Ty → Term → Prop where
    | baseNeutral {t : Term} :
        IsLongBetaNeutral .base t →
        IsLongBetaNormal .base t
    | lam (x : Var) {σ : Ty} {r : Term} :
        IsLongBetaNormal σ r →
        IsLongBetaNormal (.arr x.ty σ) (.lam x r)

  /-- Neutral spine `y s₁ ... sₖ` whose arguments are in long β-normal form. -/
  inductive IsLongBetaNeutral : Ty → Term → Prop where
    | var (y : Var) :
        IsLongBetaNeutral y.ty (.var y)
    | app {t s : Term} {σ τ : Ty} :
        IsLongBetaNeutral (.arr σ τ) t →
        IsLongBetaNormal σ s →
        IsLongBetaNeutral τ (.app t s)
end

/-- Section 2 (p. 204): Bound-variable renaming functional `α_k(r)` for `k ∈ {0, 1}*`:
- `α_k(x) = x`
- `α_k(r s) = (α_{k * 0} r)(α_{k * 1} s)`
- `α_k(λy^ρ. r) = λx_k^ρ. (α_{k * 0} r)[x_k^ρ / y^ρ]` (standardizing inner bound variables
  to indices extending `k * 0` first so that renaming `y^ρ ↦ x_k^ρ` is capture-free). -/
def alphaRename (k : Index) (r : Term) : Term :=
  match r with
  | .var x => .var x
  | .app t s =>
      .app (alphaRename (appendIdx k zeroIdx) t) (alphaRename (appendIdx k oneIdx) s)
  | .lam y body =>
      let xk := indexedVar y.ty k
      let yFresh : Var := ⟨.named (maxNamedId body + 1), y.ty⟩
      let body' := alphaRename (appendIdx k zeroIdx) (renameFreeVar body y yFresh)
      .lam xk (renameFreeVar body' yFresh xk)
termination_by rawSize r
decreasing_by
  all_goals
    simp_wf
    simp [rawSize, renameFreeVar_rawSize]
    try omega

/-- Section 2 (p. 204): Term family representation `EMB : Λ → (Index → Λ)` defined by
`EMB r k := α_k(r)`. -/
def EMB (r : Term) (k : Index) : Term :=
  alphaRename k r

/-- Maximum length among a list of 0–1 sequences. -/
def maxIdxLength : List Index → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | l :: ls => Nat.max l.length (maxIdxLength ls)

/-- Canonical fresh index `k̂(F) ∈ {0, 1}*` computed from `F(ε)` and `F(0)` (pp. 204–205):
a sequence of `0`s strictly longer than every index occurring in `F(ε)` or `F(0)`, so that
no index in `{l ∈ {0,1}* | x_l free in r}` extends `k̂`. -/
def canonicalFreshIndex (F : Index → Term) : Index :=
  let len := Nat.max (maxIdxLength (freeIndices (F epsIdx)))
                     (maxIdxLength (freeIndices (F zeroIdx))) + 1
  List.replicate len false

/-- Section 2 (p. 205): Extraction functional `EXTRACT : Λ^{{0,1}*} → Λ` defined by
`EXTRACT(F) := F(k̂)`. -/
def EXTRACT (F : Index → Term) : Term :=
  F (canonicalFreshIndex F)

end BergerSchwichtenberg1991

# Read-back: `Def_BergerSchwichtenberg1991_Syntax.lean`

**`Ty`** — Defines an inductive type of simple types built from a single ground type $o$ and a binary arrow constructor $(\rho, \sigma) \mapsto (\rho \to \sigma)$, equipped with decidable equality.

**`Ty.arrMany`** — Given a finite list of types $[\sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_k]$ and a return type $\tau$, defines the right-associated iterated function type $\sigma_1 \to (\sigma_2 \to \cdots \to (\sigma_k \to \tau)\cdots)$ by structural recursion on the list, returning $\tau$ when the list is empty.

**`Ty.argTypes`** — Given a type $\rho$, extracts its list of domain types by structural recursion: returns the empty list $[]$ when $\rho = o$, and returns $\sigma :: \mathrm{argTypes}(\tau)$ when $\rho = (\sigma \to \tau)$.

**`Index`, `epsIdx`, `zeroIdx`, `oneIdx`, `appendIdx`, and `IsPrefixOf`** — Defines an index ($\mathrm{Index}$) as a finite list of booleans $\{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^*$. The distinguished constant $\varepsilon$ (`epsIdx`) is the empty list $[]$, $0$ (`zeroIdx`) is the singleton list $[\mathrm{false}]$, and $1$ (`oneIdx`) is the singleton list $[\mathrm{true}]$. For any two indices $k, l \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^*$, $k * l$ (`appendIdx`) is their list concatenation $k \mathbin{++} l$. For any two indices $k, m \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^*$, the relation $\mathrm{IsPrefixOf}(k, m)$ holds if and only if there exists an index $l \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^*$ such that $m = k \mathbin{++} l$.

**`VarName`, `Var`, and `indexedVar`** — Defines a variable identifier ($\mathrm{VarName}$) as an inductive type with two disjoint constructors: an indexed identifier $\mathrm{indexed}(k)$ for $k \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^*$, and a named identifier $\mathrm{named}(n)$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A typed variable ($\mathrm{Var}$) is a pair $x = (\mathrm{name}, \mathrm{ty})$ consisting of an identifier $\mathrm{name} \in \mathrm{VarName}$ and a simple type $\mathrm{ty} \in \mathrm{Ty}$ (with decidable equality comparing both components, so variables with the same identifier but distinct types are distinct elements of $\mathrm{Var}$). For any type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$ and index $k \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^*$, $x_k^\rho$ (`indexedVar`) is the typed variable $(\mathrm{indexed}(k), \rho)$.

**`Term`, `Term.appMany`, and `Term.lamMany`** — Defines raw $\lambda$-terms ($\mathrm{Term}$) inductively with three constructors: a variable term $\mathrm{var}(x)$ for $x \in \mathrm{Var}$, an application $\mathrm{app}(t, r)$ for $t, r \in \mathrm{Term}$, and a $\lambda$-abstraction $\mathrm{lam}(x, r)$ for $x \in \mathrm{Var}$ and $r \in \mathrm{Term}$. Given a head term $r$ and a list of argument terms $[s_1, \dots, s_k]$, $\mathrm{appMany}(r, [s_1, \dots, s_k])$ forms the left-associated iterated application $(\cdots ((r\ s_1)\ s_2)\cdots s_k)$ (returning $r$ when the list is empty). Given a list of typed variables $[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ and a body $r$, $\mathrm{lamMany}([x_1, \dots, x_n], r)$ forms the right-nested iterated abstraction $\lambda x_1.\ \dots \lambda x_n.\ r$ (returning $r$ when the list is empty).

**`HasType`** — Defines an inductive typing relation $r : \rho$ ($\mathrm{HasType}(r, \rho)$) between a raw term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$ and a simple type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$ without an external typing context: (1) for every typed variable $x \in \mathrm{Var}$, $\mathrm{var}(x)$ has type $x.\mathrm{ty}$; (2) for all terms $t, r \in \mathrm{Term}$ and types $\rho, \sigma \in \mathrm{Ty}$, if $t : (\rho \to \sigma)$ and $r : \rho$, then $\mathrm{app}(t, r) : \sigma$; and (3) for every typed variable $x \in \mathrm{Var}$, term $s \in \mathrm{Term}$, and type $\sigma \in \mathrm{Ty}$, if $s : \sigma$, then $\mathrm{lam}(x, s) : (x.\mathrm{ty} \to \sigma)$. Because each variable occurrence carries its own intrinsic type, two free variables in a well-typed term may share the same $\mathrm{VarName}$ while having different types.

**`freeVarOccurrences`, `freeVars`, `IsClosed`, `freeIndices`, and `allVars`** — For a raw term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$, $\mathrm{freeVarOccurrences}(r)$ computes the list of free variable occurrences by structural recursion: $[x]$ for $\mathrm{var}(x)$, list concatenation $\mathrm{freeVarOccurrences}(t) \mathbin{++} \mathrm{freeVarOccurrences}(s)$ for $\mathrm{app}(t, s)$, and $\mathrm{freeVarOccurrences}(s)$ filtered to remove all occurrences equal to $x$ (in both $\mathrm{name}$ and $\mathrm{ty}$) for $\mathrm{lam}(x, s)$. The list $\mathrm{freeVars}(r)$ removes duplicate variables from $\mathrm{freeVarOccurrences}(r)$. The predicate $\mathrm{IsClosed}(r)$ holds if and only if $\mathrm{freeVars}(r) = []$. The list $\mathrm{freeIndices}(r)$ extracts every index $l \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^*$ such that $(\mathrm{indexed}(l), \sigma) \in \mathrm{freeVars}(r)$ for some type $\sigma$, ignoring all $\mathrm{named}(n)$ variables. The list $\mathrm{allVars}(r)$ collects all variables (both free occurrences and $\lambda$-binders) occurring anywhere in $r$: $[x]$ for $\mathrm{var}(x)$, $\mathrm{allVars}(t) \mathbin{++} \mathrm{allVars}(s)$ for $\mathrm{app}(t, s)$, and $x :: \mathrm{allVars}(s)$ for $\mathrm{lam}(x, s)$.

**`maxNamedId`, `maxNamedIdList`, `renameFreeVar`, `rawSize`, `renameFreeVar_rawSize`, and `substTerm`** — For a raw term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$, $\mathrm{maxNamedId}(r) \in \mathbb{N}$ computes the maximum natural number $n$ occurring in any $\mathrm{named}(n)$ variable (whether free or bound as a $\lambda$-binder) anywhere in $r$, returning $0$ if only indexed variables occur; $\mathrm{maxNamedIdList}(ts)$ returns the maximum of $\mathrm{maxNamedId}(t)$ across a list of terms $ts$ ($0$ for $[]$). For $r \in \mathrm{Term}$ and $x, y \in \mathrm{Var}$, $\mathrm{renameFreeVar}(r, x, y)$ replaces every free occurrence of $x$ in $r$ with $y$, stopping under $\mathrm{lam}(v, \mathrm{body})$ when $v = x$, without checking whether $y$ is captured by an inner binder $\mathrm{lam}(y, \dots)$ in $r$. The function $\mathrm{rawSize}(r) \in \mathbb{N}$ counts the number of AST nodes in $r$, and `renameFreeVar_rawSize` states that $\mathrm{rawSize}(\mathrm{renameFreeVar}(r, x, y)) = \mathrm{rawSize}(r)$. For $r, s \in \mathrm{Term}$ and $x \in \mathrm{Var}$, single-variable substitution $\mathrm{substTerm}(r, x, s)$ replaces free occurrences of $x$ in $r$ by $s$: on $\mathrm{var}(v)$ it returns $s$ if $v = x$ and $\mathrm{var}(v)$ otherwise; on $\mathrm{app}(t, u)$ it recurses on both subterms; and on $\mathrm{lam}(v, \mathrm{body})$ it returns $\mathrm{lam}(v, \mathrm{body})$ if $v = x$, else if $v \in \mathrm{freeVarOccurrences}(s)$ it sets
$$m = \max\bigl(\mathrm{maxNamedId}(\mathrm{body}),\, \max(\mathrm{maxNamedId}(s), \mathrm{maxNamedId}(\mathrm{var}(x)))\bigr) + 1, \qquad v' = (\mathrm{named}(m), v.\mathrm{ty}),$$
and returns $\mathrm{lam}(v', \mathrm{substTerm}(\mathrm{renameFreeVar}(\mathrm{body}, v, v'), x, s))$, and otherwise returns $\mathrm{lam}(v, \mathrm{substTerm}(\mathrm{body}, x, s))$. Note that when $v \neq x$ and $v \in \mathrm{freeVarOccurrences}(s)$, $v$ is renamed to $v'$ even if $x \notin \mathrm{freeVars}(\mathrm{body})$.

**`Substitution`, `IsWellTypedSubst`, `idSubst`, `updateSubst`, and `applySubst`** — Defines a substitution ($\mathrm{Substitution}$) as a total function $\theta : \mathrm{Var} \to \mathrm{Term}$. The predicate $\mathrm{IsWellTypedSubst}(\theta)$ holds if and only if $\forall x \in \mathrm{Var},\; \mathrm{HasType}(\theta(x), x.\mathrm{ty})$. The identity substitution $\mathrm{idSubst}$ maps each $x \in \mathrm{Var}$ to $\mathrm{var}(x)$, and $\mathrm{updateSubst}(\theta, x, t)$ maps $y$ to $t$ if $y = x$ and to $\theta(y)$ otherwise. For $\theta : \mathrm{Var} \to \mathrm{Term}$ and $r \in \mathrm{Term}$, simultaneous capture-avoiding substitution $\mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, r)$ is defined by structural recursion on $r$:
- $\mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, \mathrm{var}(x)) = \theta(x)$;
- $\mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, \mathrm{app}(t, u)) = \mathrm{app}(\mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, t), \mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, u))$;
- for $\mathrm{lam}(v, \mathrm{body})$, let $\mathrm{fvBody} = \{u \in \mathrm{freeVars}(\mathrm{body}) \mid u \neq v\}$, $\mathrm{imgTerms} = [\theta(u) \mid u \in \mathrm{fvBody}]$, and $\mathrm{imgFVs}$ be the concatenated list of $\mathrm{freeVarOccurrences}(t)$ for $t \in \mathrm{imgTerms}$:
  - if $v \in \mathrm{imgFVs}$, it sets $m = \max(\mathrm{maxNamedId}(\mathrm{body}), \max(\mathrm{maxNamedId}(\mathrm{var}(v)), \mathrm{maxNamedIdList}(\mathrm{imgTerms}))) + 1$ and $v' = (\mathrm{named}(m), v.\mathrm{ty})$, and returns
    $$\mathrm{lam}\bigl(v',\, \mathrm{applySubst}(\mathrm{updateSubst}(\theta, v, \mathrm{var}(v')),\, \mathrm{body})\bigr);$$
  - otherwise, it returns $\mathrm{lam}(v, \mathrm{applySubst}(\mathrm{updateSubst}(\theta, v, \mathrm{var}(v)), \mathrm{body}))$.

**`AlphaEq`** — Defines $\alpha$-equivalence $r =_\alpha s$ ($\mathrm{AlphaEq}(r, s)$) as the smallest equivalence relation on $\mathrm{Term}$ closed under application congruence ($\mathrm{app}$), $\lambda$-body congruence ($\mathrm{lam\_congr}$), and the renaming rule ($\mathrm{lam\_rename}$): for any variables $x, y \in \mathrm{Var}$ and raw term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$, if $x.\mathrm{ty} = y.\mathrm{ty}$ and either $y = x$ or $y \notin \mathrm{allVars}(r)$, then
$$\mathrm{lam}(x, r) =_\alpha \mathrm{lam}(y, \mathrm{renameFreeVar}(r, x, y)).$$

**`BetaEtaEq`** — Defines $\beta\eta$-equality $r =_{\beta\eta} s$ ($\mathrm{BetaEtaEq}(r, s)$) on raw terms $r, s \in \mathrm{Term}$ as the smallest equivalence relation containing $\mathrm{AlphaEq}$, closed under application congruence ($\mathrm{app}$) and $\lambda$-abstraction congruence ($\mathrm{lam}$), and satisfying: (1) for all $x \in \mathrm{Var}$ and $r, s \in \mathrm{Term}$, $\mathrm{app}(\mathrm{lam}(x, r), s) =_{\beta\eta} \mathrm{substTerm}(r, x, s)$ ($\mathrm{beta}$); and (2) for all $x \in \mathrm{Var}$ and $r \in \mathrm{Term}$ with $x \notin \mathrm{freeVars}(r)$, $\mathrm{lam}(x, \mathrm{app}(r, \mathrm{var}(x))) =_{\beta\eta} r$ ($\mathrm{eta}$). Neither $\mathrm{beta}$ nor $\mathrm{eta}$ imposes a typing hypothesis on $r$ or $s$.

**`IsLongBetaNormal` and `IsLongBetaNeutral`** — Defines two mutually inductive predicates relating a type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$ and a raw term $t \in \mathrm{Term}$:
- $\mathrm{IsLongBetaNormal}(\rho, t)$ holds either when $\rho = o$ and $\mathrm{IsLongBetaNeutral}(o, t)$ ($\mathrm{baseNeutral}$), or when $t = \mathrm{lam}(x, r)$ and $\rho = (x.\mathrm{ty} \to \sigma)$ for some $x \in \mathrm{Var}$, $\sigma \in \mathrm{Ty}$, and $r \in \mathrm{Term}$ satisfying $\mathrm{IsLongBetaNormal}(\sigma, r)$ ($\mathrm{lam}$).
- $\mathrm{IsLongBetaNeutral}(\tau, t)$ holds either when $t = \mathrm{var}(y)$ and $\tau = y.\mathrm{ty}$ for some $y \in \mathrm{Var}$ ($\mathrm{var}$), or when $t = \mathrm{app}(u, s)$ for some $u, s \in \mathrm{Term}$ and $\sigma \in \mathrm{Ty}$ such that $\mathrm{IsLongBetaNeutral}(\sigma \to \tau, u)$ and $\mathrm{IsLongBetaNormal}(\sigma, s)$ ($\mathrm{app}$).

**`alphaRename`, `EMB`, `maxIdxLength`, `canonicalFreshIndex`, and `EXTRACT`** — For an index $k \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^*$ and a raw term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$, $\alpha_k(r)$ ($\mathrm{alphaRename}(k, r)$) is defined by structural recursion on $\mathrm{rawSize}(r)$:
$$\alpha_k(\mathrm{var}(x)) = \mathrm{var}(x), \qquad \alpha_k(\mathrm{app}(t, s)) = \mathrm{app}(\alpha_{k * 0}(t), \alpha_{k * 1}(s)),$$
$$\alpha_k(\mathrm{lam}(y, \mathrm{body})) = \mathrm{lam}\Bigl(x_k^{y.\mathrm{ty}},\, \mathrm{renameFreeVar}\bigl(\alpha_{k * 0}(\mathrm{renameFreeVar}(\mathrm{body}, y, y_{\mathrm{fresh}})),\, y_{\mathrm{fresh}},\, x_k^{y.\mathrm{ty}}\bigr)\Bigr),$$
where $y_{\mathrm{fresh}} = (\mathrm{named}(\mathrm{maxNamedId}(\mathrm{body}) + 1), y.\mathrm{ty})$ is a fresh named variable not occurring anywhere in $\mathrm{body}$. The embedding functional $\mathrm{EMB} : \mathrm{Term} \to (\mathrm{Index} \to \mathrm{Term})$ is defined by $\mathrm{EMB}(r)(k) = \alpha_k(r)$. For a list of indices $ls$, $\mathrm{maxIdxLength}(ls) \in \mathbb{N}$ returns the maximum length among the lists in $ls$ (or $0$ if $ls = []$). For any term family $F : \mathrm{Index} \to \mathrm{Term}$, $\mathrm{canonicalFreshIndex}(F)$ is the boolean list $[\mathrm{false}, \dots, \mathrm{false}]$ ($0^\ell$) of length
$$\ell = \max\bigl(\mathrm{maxIdxLength}(\mathrm{freeIndices}(F(\varepsilon))),\, \mathrm{maxIdxLength}(\mathrm{freeIndices}(F(0)))\bigr) + 1,$$
and $\mathrm{EXTRACT}(F) = F(\mathrm{canonicalFreshIndex}(F))$.

import Definitions.Def_BergerSchwichtenberg1991_Syntax

/-!
# Admissible λ-Models, pr-Models, and the Inversion Functional (Berger–Schwichtenberg 1991, Sections 1, 3–5)

Source: Ulrich Berger and Helmut Schwichtenberg,
"An inverse of the evaluation functional for typed λ-calculus",
*LICS 1991*, pp. 203–211, Sections 1, 3, 4, 5 (pp. 204–208).

This module formalizes:
- Section 1: Extensional pre-structures and λ-models (`LambdaModel`, p. 204), environments (`Env`),
  evaluation `|r|η`, and semantic validity `ModelsEq` (`M ⊨ r = s`).
- Section 3: Admissible λ-models (`AdmissibleModel`, p. 205), primitive recursive functions
  and pr-models (`PRModel`, p. 206), and auxiliary operations `f_extract`, `f_app`, `fam`
  (Lemma 4, p. 206).
- Section 4: The mutually recursive reification/reflection functionals `Φ_ρ` (`Phi`) and `Ψ_ρ`
  (`Psi`, p. 207), the substitution environment `η_θ` (`etaSubst`), the procedure-to-expression
  inversion relation `pe_ρ` (`IsPeResult`, p. 207), and `inv_ρ` (`invCode`) for pr-models (p. 208).
-/

namespace BergerSchwichtenberg1991

universe u

/-- Section 1 (p. 204): An extensional λ-model `M = (M^ρ, A_{ρ,σ}, =_ρ, |·|·)` consists of:
- a carrier `Dom ρ` (`M^ρ`) for each type `ρ`,
- application mappings `appM ρ σ : M^{ρ→σ} → M^ρ → M^σ`,
- equivalence relations `eqM ρ` (`=_ρ`) that are congruences for `appM` and satisfy
  extensionality (`∀ b ∈ M^ρ, a b =_σ a' b ⇒ a =_{ρ→σ} a'`),
- an evaluation mapping `eval r η ∈ M^ρ` satisfying the variable, application, and abstraction
  laws of a λ-model, and respecting α-equivalence. -/
structure LambdaModel where
  Dom : Ty → Type u
  appM : {ρ σ : Ty} → Dom (.arr ρ σ) → Dom ρ → Dom σ
  eqM : (ρ : Ty) → Dom ρ → Dom ρ → Prop
  eqM_refl : ∀ (ρ : Ty) (a : Dom ρ), eqM ρ a a
  eqM_symm : ∀ (ρ : Ty) {a b : Dom ρ}, eqM ρ a b → eqM ρ b a
  eqM_trans : ∀ (ρ : Ty) {a b c : Dom ρ}, eqM ρ a b → eqM ρ b c → eqM ρ a c
  appM_congr : ∀ {ρ σ : Ty} {f f' : Dom (.arr ρ σ)} {a a' : Dom ρ},
      eqM (.arr ρ σ) f f' → eqM ρ a a' → eqM σ (appM f a) (appM f' a')
  extensional : ∀ {ρ σ : Ty} {f f' : Dom (.arr ρ σ)},
      (∀ b : Dom ρ, eqM σ (appM f b) (appM f' b)) → eqM (.arr ρ σ) f f'
  eval : Term → (∀ x : Var, Dom x.ty) → (ρ : Ty) → Dom ρ
  eval_var : ∀ (x : Var) (η : ∀ v : Var, Dom v.ty),
      eqM x.ty (eval (.var x) η x.ty) (η x)
  eval_app : ∀ (t r : Term) (ρ σ : Ty) (η : ∀ v : Var, Dom v.ty),
      HasType t (.arr ρ σ) → HasType r ρ →
      eqM σ (eval (.app t r) η σ) (appM (eval t η (.arr ρ σ)) (eval r η ρ))
  eval_lam : ∀ (x : Var) (s : Term) (σ : Ty) (η : ∀ v : Var, Dom v.ty) (a : Dom x.ty),
      HasType s σ →
      eqM σ (appM (eval (.lam x s) η (.arr x.ty σ)) a)
            (eval s (fun y => if h : y = x then h ▸ a else η y) σ)
  eval_congr_env : ∀ (r : Term) (ρ : Ty) (η₁ η₂ : ∀ v : Var, Dom v.ty),
      HasType r ρ →
      (∀ v ∈ freeVars r, eqM v.ty (η₁ v) (η₂ v)) →
      eqM ρ (eval r η₁ ρ) (eval r η₂ ρ)
  eval_alpha : ∀ {r s : Term} (ρ : Ty) (η : ∀ v : Var, Dom v.ty),
      HasType r ρ → AlphaEq r s →
      eqM ρ (eval r η ρ) (eval s η ρ)

namespace LambdaModel

/-- Environment `ENV` mapping each typed variable `x^ρ` to `M^ρ` (p. 204). -/
abbrev Env (M : LambdaModel.{u}) := ∀ x : Var, M.Dom x.ty

/-- Environment update `η[x ↦ a]` (p. 204). -/
def updateEnv (M : LambdaModel.{u}) (η : M.Env) (x : Var) (a : M.Dom x.ty) : M.Env :=
  fun y => if h : y = x then h ▸ a else η y

/-- Default evaluation `|r|` of a closed term `r ∈ Λ^ρ` (independent of the environment `η`
by `eval_congr_env`). -/
def evalIn (M : LambdaModel.{u}) (r : Term) (ρ : Ty) (η : M.Env) : M.Dom ρ :=
  M.eval r η ρ

/-- `M ⊨_η r = s` holds if `|r|η =_ρ |s|η` in `M` (Section 1, p. 204). -/
def ModelsEqAt (M : LambdaModel.{u}) (ρ : Ty) (η : M.Env) (r s : Term) : Prop :=
  M.eqM ρ (M.eval r η ρ) (M.eval s η ρ)

/-- `M ⊨ r = s` holds if `∀ η : ENV, M ⊨_η r = s` (Section 1, p. 204). -/
def ModelsEq (M : LambdaModel.{u}) (ρ : Ty) (r s : Term) : Prop :=
  ∀ η : M.Env, M.ModelsEqAt ρ η r s

/-- An element `a ∈ M^ρ` is λ-definable (with respect to environment `η` on closed terms)
if there is a closed term `r ∈ Λ^ρ` such that `|r| =_ρ a` (Section 4, p. 207). -/
def IsLambdaDefinable (M : LambdaModel.{u}) (ρ : Ty) (a : M.Dom ρ) : Prop :=
  ∃ r : Term, HasType r ρ ∧ IsClosed r ∧ ∀ η : M.Env, M.eqM ρ (M.eval r η ρ) a

end LambdaModel

/-- Section 3 (p. 205): An admissible λ-model `M` is a λ-model equipped with types `f` (term
families) and `ι` (indices), coding functions `⌈·⌉^o : Λ → M^o` and `⌈·⌉^ι : {0,1}* → M^ι`,
and objects `append`, `mvar_ρ`, `app`, `abst_ρ`, `emb`, `fun`, `extract` satisfying the
admissibility axioms `(append)`, `(mvar)`, `(app)`, `(abst)`, `(⌈·⌉)`, `(emb)`, `(fun)`,
and `(extract)`. -/
structure AdmissibleModel extends LambdaModel.{u} where
  tyF : Ty
  tyIdx : Ty
  codeTerm : Term → Dom .base
  codeIdx : Index → Dom tyIdx
  append : Dom (.arr tyIdx (.arr tyIdx tyIdx))
  mvar : (ρ : Ty) → Dom (.arr tyIdx .base)
  appCode : Dom (.arr .base (.arr .base .base))
  abst : (ρ : Ty) → Dom (.arr tyIdx (.arr .base .base))
  emb : Dom (.arr .base tyF)
  funOp : Dom (.arr tyF (.arr tyIdx .base))
  extract : Dom (.arr (.arr tyIdx .base) .base)
  /-- `(append)`: `append ⌈k⌉ ⌈l⌉ =_ι ⌈k * l⌉` -/
  law_append : ∀ k l : Index,
      eqM tyIdx (appM (appM append (codeIdx k)) (codeIdx l)) (codeIdx (appendIdx k l))
  /-- `(mvar)`: `mvar_ρ ⌈k⌉ =_o ⌈x_k^ρ⌉` -/
  law_mvar : ∀ (ρ : Ty) (k : Index),
      eqM .base (appM (mvar ρ) (codeIdx k)) (codeTerm (.var (indexedVar ρ k)))
  /-- `(app)`: `app ⌈r⌉ ⌈s⌉ =_o ⌈r s⌉` -/
  law_app : ∀ r s : Term,
      eqM .base (appM (appM appCode (codeTerm r)) (codeTerm s)) (codeTerm (.app r s))
  /-- `(abst)`: `abst_ρ ⌈k⌉ ⌈r⌉ =_o ⌈λx_k^ρ. r⌉` -/
  law_abst : ∀ (ρ : Ty) (k : Index) (r : Term),
      eqM .base (appM (appM (abst ρ) (codeIdx k)) (codeTerm r))
        (codeTerm (.lam (indexedVar ρ k) r))
  /-- `(⌈·⌉)`: `⌈r⌉ =_o ⌈s⌉ ⇒ EMB r = EMB s` -/
  law_code_inj : ∀ r s : Term,
      eqM .base (codeTerm r) (codeTerm s) → EMB r = EMB s
  /-- `(emb)`: `EMB r = EMB s ⇒ emb ⌈r⌉ =_f emb ⌈s⌉` -/
  law_emb_congr : ∀ r s : Term,
      EMB r = EMB s → eqM tyF (appM emb (codeTerm r)) (appM emb (codeTerm s))
  /-- `(fun)`: `fun (emb ⌈r⌉) ⌈k⌉ =_o ⌈EMB r k⌉` -/
  law_fun : ∀ (r : Term) (k : Index),
      eqM .base (appM (appM funOp (appM emb (codeTerm r))) (codeIdx k))
        (codeTerm (EMB r k))
  /-- `(extract)`: `(∀ k, a ⌈k⌉ =_o ⌈EMB r k⌉) ⇒ extract(a) =_o ⌈EXTRACT(EMB r)⌉` -/
  law_extract : ∀ (a : Dom (.arr tyIdx .base)) (r : Term),
      (∀ k : Index, eqM .base (appM a (codeIdx k)) (codeTerm (EMB r k))) →
      eqM .base (appM extract a) (codeTerm (EXTRACT (EMB r)))
  /-- Closure of `M` under the λ-definable step combinator used in `Φ_{ρ→σ}` (Section 4, p. 207):
      for every transformation `body : M^ι → M^f`, the functional
      `p ↦ abst_ρ p (fun (body p) (append p ⌈0⌉))` is represented by an element of `M^{ι→o}`
      whenever `body` comes from `a : M^{ρ→σ}`, `Ψ_ρ : M^f → M^ρ`, and `Φ_σ : M^σ → M^f`. -/
  mkStepFun : (ρ : Ty) → (Dom tyIdx → Dom tyF) → Dom (.arr tyIdx .base)
  mkStepFun_spec : ∀ (ρ : Ty) (body : Dom tyIdx → Dom tyF) (p : Dom tyIdx),
      (∀ p₁ p₂ : Dom tyIdx, eqM tyIdx p₁ p₂ → eqM tyF (body p₁) (body p₂)) →
      eqM .base (appM (mkStepFun ρ body) p)
        (appM (appM (abst ρ) p)
          (appM (appM funOp (body p)) (appM (appM append p) (codeIdx zeroIdx))))

namespace AdmissibleModel

variable (M : AdmissibleModel.{u})

/-- Section 3 (p. 206): `f-extract f = extract (fun f)`. -/
def f_extract (f : M.Dom M.tyF) : M.Dom .base :=
  M.appM M.extract (M.appM M.funOp f)

/-- Section 3 (p. 206): `f-app f g = emb (app (f-extract f) (f-extract g))`. -/
def f_app (f g : M.Dom M.tyF) : M.Dom M.tyF :=
  M.appM M.emb (M.appM (M.appM M.appCode (M.f_extract f)) (M.f_extract g))

/-- Section 3 (p. 206): `fam(a) = emb (extract(a))`. -/
def fam (a : M.Dom (.arr M.tyIdx .base)) : M.Dom M.tyF :=
  M.appM M.emb (M.appM M.extract a)

end AdmissibleModel

/-- Structure packaging the interpreted λ-terms `Φ_ρ ∈ M^{ρ→f}` and `Ψ_ρ ∈ M^{f→ρ}` defined by
the recursion equations of Section 4 (p. 207) in an admissible model `M`:
- `Φ_o = emb`
- `Ψ_o = f-extract`
- `Φ_{ρ→σ}(a) = fam(λp^ι. abst_ρ p (fun (Φ_σ (a (Ψ_ρ (emb (mvar_ρ p))))) (append p ⌈0⌉)))`
- `Ψ_{ρ→σ}(f)(a) = Ψ_σ (f-app f (Φ_ρ a))`. -/
structure InversionFunctionals (M : AdmissibleModel.{u}) where
  Phi : (ρ : Ty) → M.Dom (.arr ρ M.tyF)
  Psi : (ρ : Ty) → M.Dom (.arr M.tyF ρ)
  phi_base : ∀ a : M.Dom .base,
      M.eqM M.tyF (M.appM (Phi .base) a) (M.appM M.emb a)
  psi_base : ∀ f : M.Dom M.tyF,
      M.eqM .base (M.appM (Psi .base) f) (M.f_extract f)
  phi_arr : ∀ (ρ σ : Ty) (a : M.Dom (.arr ρ σ)),
      ∃ step : M.Dom (.arr M.tyIdx .base),
        (∀ p : M.Dom M.tyIdx,
          M.eqM .base (M.appM step p)
            (M.appM (M.appM (M.abst ρ) p)
              (M.appM
                (M.appM M.funOp
                  (M.appM (Phi σ)
                    (M.appM a (M.appM (Psi ρ) (M.appM M.emb (M.appM (M.mvar ρ) p))))))
                (M.appM (M.appM M.append p) (M.codeIdx zeroIdx))))) ∧
        M.eqM M.tyF (M.appM (Phi (.arr ρ σ)) a) (M.fam step)
  psi_arr : ∀ (ρ σ : Ty) (f : M.Dom M.tyF) (a : M.Dom ρ),
      M.eqM σ (M.appM (M.appM (Psi (.arr ρ σ)) f) a)
        (M.appM (Psi σ) (M.f_app f (M.appM (Phi ρ) a)))

namespace InversionFunctionals

variable {M : AdmissibleModel.{u}} (IF : InversionFunctionals M)

/-- Section 4 (p. 207): For any substitution `θ`, the environment `η_θ ∈ ENV` is defined by
`η_θ(y^ρ) = Ψ_ρ(emb(⌈θ y^ρ⌉))`. -/
def etaSubst (θ : Substitution) : M.Env :=
  fun y => M.appM (IF.Psi y.ty) (M.appM M.emb (M.codeTerm (θ y)))

/-- Environment `η_id` corresponding to the identity substitution `θ_id(y) = y` (p. 207). -/
def etaId : M.Env :=
  IF.etaSubst idSubst

/-- Section 4 (p. 207): Partial inversion functional `p-e_ρ(a) ≃ (f-extract(Φ_ρ(a)))^~`:
`IsPeResult ρ a t` holds if `t ∈ Λ^ρ` and `⌈t⌉ =_o f-extract(Φ_ρ(a))`. -/
def IsPeResult (ρ : Ty) (a : M.Dom ρ) (t : Term) : Prop :=
  HasType t ρ ∧ M.eqM .base (M.codeTerm t) (M.f_extract (M.appM (IF.Phi ρ) a))

/-- Code-level inversion functional `inv_ρ(a) := f-extract(Φ_ρ(a)) ∈ M^o` (p. 208). -/
def invCode (ρ : Ty) (a : M.Dom ρ) : M.Dom .base :=
  M.f_extract (M.appM (IF.Phi ρ) a)

end InversionFunctionals

/-- Inductive characterization of primitive recursive functions `ℕ^k → ℕ` (Section 3, p. 206). -/
inductive IsPrimRec : {k : Nat} → ((Fin k → Nat) → Nat) → Prop where
  | zero : IsPrimRec (k := 1) (fun _ => 0)
  | succ : IsPrimRec (k := 1) (fun v => v ⟨0, by decide⟩ + 1)
  | proj {k : Nat} (i : Fin k) : IsPrimRec (k := k) (fun v => v i)
  | comp {k m : Nat} {g : (Fin m → Nat) → Nat} {hs : Fin m → (Fin k → Nat) → Nat} :
      IsPrimRec g →
      (∀ j : Fin m, IsPrimRec (hs j)) →
      IsPrimRec (k := k) (fun v => g (fun j => hs j v))
  | prec {k : Nat} {g : (Fin k → Nat) → Nat} {h : (Fin (k + 2) → Nat) → Nat} :
      IsPrimRec g →
      IsPrimRec h →
      IsPrimRec (k := k + 1) (fun v =>
        Nat.rec
          (g (fun i => v ⟨i.val + 1, by omega⟩))
          (fun y ih =>
            h (fun j =>
              if _hj0 : j.val = 0 then y
              else if _hj1 : j.val = 1 then ih
              else v ⟨j.val - 1, by omega⟩))
          (v ⟨0, by omega⟩))

/-- Binary function `h : Nat → Nat → Nat` is primitive recursive (Section 3, p. 206). -/
def IsBinaryPrimRec (h : Nat → Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  IsPrimRec (k := 2) (fun v => h (v ⟨0, by decide⟩) (v ⟨1, by decide⟩))

/-- Unary function `f : Nat → Nat` is primitive recursive (Section 3, p. 206). -/
def IsUnaryPrimRec (f : Nat → Nat) : Prop :=
  IsPrimRec (k := 1) (fun v => f (v ⟨0, by decide⟩))

/-- Section 3 (p. 206): A λ-model `M` is a `pr-model` if all unary and binary primitive
recursive functions are represented in `M` via an injection `ν : ω → M^o` (with respect to `=_o`). -/
structure PRModel extends LambdaModel.{u} where
  nu : Nat → Dom .base
  nu_inj : ∀ n m : Nat, eqM .base (nu n) (nu m) → n = m
  reprUnary : ∀ f : Nat → Nat, IsUnaryPrimRec f →
      ∃ fBar : Dom (.arr .base .base),
        ∀ n : Nat, eqM .base (appM fBar (nu n)) (nu (f n))
  reprBinary : ∀ h : Nat → Nat → Nat, IsBinaryPrimRec h →
      ∃ hBar : Dom (.arr .base (.arr .base .base)),
        ∀ n m : Nat, eqM .base (appM (appM hBar (nu n)) (nu m)) (nu (h n m))

/-- Effective repetition-free numbering of terms `Λ` and indices `{0,1}*` (Section 3, p. 206). -/
structure EffectiveNumbering where
  termOfNat : Nat → Term
  natOfTerm : Term → Nat
  idxOfNat : Nat → Index
  natOfIdx : Index → Nat
  term_left_inv : ∀ r : Term, termOfNat (natOfTerm r) = r
  term_right_inv : ∀ n : Nat, natOfTerm (termOfNat n) = n
  idx_left_inv : ∀ k : Index, idxOfNat (natOfIdx k) = k
  idx_right_inv : ∀ n : Nat, natOfIdx (idxOfNat n) = n
  append_prim : IsBinaryPrimRec (fun n m => natOfIdx (appendIdx (idxOfNat n) (idxOfNat m)))
  mvar_prim : ∀ ρ : Ty, IsUnaryPrimRec (fun n => natOfTerm (.var (indexedVar ρ (idxOfNat n))))
  app_prim : IsBinaryPrimRec (fun n m => natOfTerm (.app (termOfNat n) (termOfNat m)))
  abst_prim : ∀ ρ : Ty, IsBinaryPrimRec (fun n m =>
      natOfTerm (.lam (indexedVar ρ (idxOfNat n)) (termOfNat m)))
  exemb_prim : IsUnaryPrimRec (fun n => natOfTerm (EXTRACT (EMB (termOfNat n))))
  alpha_prim : IsBinaryPrimRec (fun n m => natOfTerm (EMB (termOfNat n) (idxOfNat m)))
  indext_prim : ∃ indext : Nat → Nat → Nat,
      IsBinaryPrimRec indext ∧
      ∀ r : Term,
        let n := natOfTerm (EMB r epsIdx)
        let m := natOfTerm (EMB r zeroIdx)
        EXTRACT (EMB r) = EMB r (idxOfNat (indext n m))

end BergerSchwichtenberg1991

   $$\mathrm{EXTRACT}(\mathrm{EMB}(r)) =_\alpha r.$$

items.formal_statement:
namespace BergerSchwichtenberg1991

universe u

theorem lemma_3 (M : PRModel.{u}) (N : EffectiveNumbering)
    (hExtractComb :
      ∀ indextBar : M.Dom (.arr .base (.arr .base .base)),
        ∃ extractBar : M.Dom (.arr (.arr .base .base) .base),
          ∀ a : M.Dom (.arr .base .base),
            M.eqM .base (M.appM extractBar a)
              (M.appM a
                (M.appM
                  (M.appM indextBar (M.appM a (M.nu (N.natOfIdx epsIdx))))
                  (M.appM a (M.nu (N.natOfIdx zeroIdx))))))
    (hStepComb :
      ∀ (abstBar : Ty → M.Dom (.arr .base (.arr .base .base)))
        (funBar appendBar : M.Dom (.arr .base (.arr .base .base)))
        (ρ : Ty) (body : M.Dom .base → M.Dom .base),
        (∀ p₁ p₂ : M.Dom .base, M.eqM .base p₁ p₂ → M.eqM .base (body p₁) (body p₂)) →
        ∃ step : M.Dom (.arr .base .base),
          ∀ p : M.Dom .base,
            M.eqM .base (M.appM step p)
              (M.appM (M.appM (abstBar ρ) p)
                (M.appM (M.appM funBar (body p))
                  (M.appM (M.appM appendBar p) (M.nu (N.natOfIdx zeroIdx)))))) :
    ∃ A : AdmissibleModel.{u},
      A.toLambdaModel = M.toLambdaModel ∧
      A.tyF = .base ∧
      A.tyIdx = .base ∧
      (∀ r : Term, HEq (A.codeTerm r) (M.nu (N.natOfTerm r))) ∧
      (∀ k : Index, HEq (A.codeIdx k) (M.nu (N.natOfIdx k))) := by sorry

end BergerSchwichtenberg1991

**`lemma_3`** — Given a primitive recursive $\lambda$-model $M : \mathrm{PRModel}$ in universe $u$ (with carrier family $M^\rho$, application $\mathrm{appM}$, equivalence $=_\rho$, evaluation $\mathrm{eval}$, and numeral injection $\nu : \mathbb{N} \to M^o$ representing all unary and binary primitive recursive functions) and an effective numbering $N : \mathrm{EffectiveNumbering}$ (providing mutually inverse bijections $\mathrm{termOfNat} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{natOfTerm}$ on $\mathrm{Term}$ and $\mathrm{idxOfNat} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{natOfIdx}$ on $\mathrm{Index}$ under which the syntactic operations are primitive recursive), together with two explicit combinator-existence hypotheses:
1. (`hExtractComb`) for every binary operation $\overline{\mathrm{indext}} \in M^{o \to o \to o}$, there exists an element $\overline{\mathrm{extract}} \in M^{(o \to o) \to o}$ such that for all $a \in M^{o \to o}$,
   $$\overline{\mathrm{extract}}\ a =_o a\ \Bigl(\overline{\mathrm{indext}}\ \bigl(a\ (\nu(\mathrm{natOfIdx}(\varepsilon)))\bigr)\ \bigl(a\ (\nu(\mathrm{natOfIdx}(0)))\bigr)\Bigr);$$
2. (`hStepComb`) for every type-indexed family $\overline{\mathrm{abst}} : \mathrm{Ty} \to M^{o \to o \to o}$, elements $\overline{\mathrm{fun}}, \overline{\mathrm{append}} \in M^{o \to o \to o}$, simple type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$, and meta-level function $\mathrm{body} : M^o \to M^o$ satisfying $\forall p_1, p_2 \in M^o,\; p_1 =_o p_2 \implies \mathrm{body}(p_1) =_o \mathrm{body}(p_2)$, there exists $\mathrm{step} \in M^{o \to o}$ such that for all $p \in M^o$,
   $$\mathrm{step}\ p =_o \overline{\mathrm{abst}}_\rho\ p\ \Bigl(\overline{\mathrm{fun}}\ (\mathrm{body}(p))\ \bigl(\overline{\mathrm{append}}\ p\ (\nu(\mathrm{natOfIdx}(0)))\bigr)\Bigr);$$

the theorem asserts that there exists an admissible model $A : \mathrm{AdmissibleModel}$ in universe $u$ such that:
- $A$'s underlying $\mathrm{LambdaModel}$ equals $M$'s underlying $\mathrm{LambdaModel}$ ($A.\mathrm{toLambdaModel} = M.\mathrm{toLambdaModel}$);
- both the term-family type and the index type of $A$ are the ground type $o$ ($A.\mathrm{tyF} = o$ and $A.\mathrm{tyIdx} = o$);
- for every raw term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$, $A.\mathrm{codeTerm}(r)$ is heterogeneously equal ($\mathrm{HEq}$) to $M.\nu(N.\mathrm{natOfTerm}(r))$; and
- for every binary index $k \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^*$, $A.\mathrm{codeIdx}(k)$ is heterogeneously equal ($\mathrm{HEq}$) to $M.\nu(N.\mathrm{natOfIdx}(k))$.

Note that the existence of the higher-order extraction combinator $\overline{\mathrm{extract}} \in M^{(o \to o) \to o}$ and the step combinators $\mathrm{step} \in M^{o \to o}$ (for arbitrary $=_o$-respecting meta-level functions $\mathrm{body} : M^o \to M^o$) is assumed via the hypotheses `hExtractComb` and `hStepComb` rather than derived solely from the fields of `PRModel` and `EffectiveNumbering`.

namespace BergerSchwichtenberg1991

universe u

theorem lemma_4 (M : AdmissibleModel.{u}) :
    (∀ r : Term,
      M.eqM .base (M.f_extract (M.appM M.emb (M.codeTerm r)))
        (M.codeTerm (EXTRACT (EMB r)))) ∧
    (∀ r : Term,
      M.eqM M.tyF (M.appM M.emb (M.f_extract (M.appM M.emb (M.codeTerm r))))
        (M.appM M.emb (M.codeTerm r))) ∧
    (∀ r s : Term,
      M.eqM M.tyF
        (M.f_app (M.appM M.emb (M.codeTerm r)) (M.appM M.emb (M.codeTerm s)))
        (M.appM M.emb (M.codeTerm (.app r s)))) ∧
    (∀ (a : M.Dom (.arr M.tyIdx .base)) (r : Term),
      (∀ k : Index, M.eqM .base (M.appM a (M.codeIdx k)) (M.codeTerm (EMB r k))) →
      M.eqM M.tyF (M.fam a) (M.appM M.emb (M.codeTerm r))) := by sorry

end BergerSchwichtenberg1991

**`lemma_4`** — For every admissible model $M : \mathrm{AdmissibleModel}$ in universe $u$ (with distinguished types $f = M.\mathrm{tyF}$ and $\iota = M.\mathrm{tyIdx}$, term coding $\lceil \cdot \rceil^o : \mathrm{Term} \to M^o$, index coding $\lceil \cdot \rceil^\iota : \mathrm{Index} \to M^\iota$, and operations $\mathrm{emb} \in M^{o \to f}$, $\mathrm{funOp} \in M^{f \to \iota \to o}$, $\mathrm{extract} \in M^{(\iota \to o) \to o}$, and $\mathrm{appCode} \in M^{o \to o \to o}$), asserts the conjunction of four equations for arbitrary raw terms (without `HasType` hypotheses):
1. For every raw term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$, applying $\mathrm{f\_extract}(u) = \mathrm{extract}\ (\mathrm{funOp}\ u)$ to $\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil r \rceil^o$ yields the code of $\mathrm{EXTRACT}(\mathrm{EMB}(r))$ up to $=_o$:
   $$\mathrm{f\_extract}(\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil r \rceil^o) =_o \lceil \mathrm{EXTRACT}(\mathrm{EMB}(r)) \rceil^o.$$
2. For every raw term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$, re-embedding $\mathrm{f\_extract}(\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil r \rceil^o)$ equals $\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil r \rceil^o$ up to $=_f$:
   $$\mathrm{emb}\bigl(\mathrm{f\_extract}(\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil r \rceil^o)\bigr) =_f \mathrm{emb}\ \lceil r \rceil^o.$$
3. For all raw terms $r, s \in \mathrm{Term}$, applying $\mathrm{f\_app}(u, v) = \mathrm{emb}\bigl(\mathrm{appCode}\ (\mathrm{f\_extract}(u))\ (\mathrm{f\_extract}(v))\bigr)$ to $\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil r \rceil^o$ and $\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil s \rceil^o$ yields $\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil \mathrm{app}(r, s) \rceil^o$ up to $=_f$:
   $$\mathrm{f\_app}(\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil r \rceil^o, \mathrm{emb}\ \lceil s \rceil^o) =_f \mathrm{emb}\ \lceil \mathrm{app}(r, s) \rceil^o.$$
4. For every element $a \in M^{\iota \to o}$ and every raw term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$, if $a\ \lceil k \rceil^\iota =_o \lceil \mathrm{EMB}(r)(k) \rceil^o$ holds for every binary index $k \in \{\mathrm{false}, \mathrm{true}\}^*$, then $\mathrm{fam}(a) = \mathrm{emb}(\mathrm{extract}\ a)$ equals $\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil r \rceil^o$ up to $=_f$:
   $$\bigl(\forall k \in \mathrm{Index},\; a\ \lceil k \rceil^\iota =_o \lceil \mathrm{EMB}(r)(k) \rceil^o\bigr) \implies \mathrm{fam}(a) =_f \mathrm{emb}\ \lceil r \rceil^o.$$

namespace BergerSchwichtenberg1991

universe u

theorem lemma_5 (M : AdmissibleModel.{u}) (IF : InversionFunctionals M)
    {ρ : Ty} {r : Term} (θ : Substitution)
    (ht : HasType r ρ)
    (hnorm : IsLongBetaNormal ρ r)
    (hθ : IsWellTypedSubst θ) :
    M.eqM M.tyF
      (M.appM (IF.Phi ρ) (M.eval r (IF.etaSubst θ) ρ))
      (M.appM M.emb (M.codeTerm (applySubst θ r))) ∧
    (∀ hbase : ρ = .base,
      M.eqM .base
        (hbase ▸ M.eval r (IF.etaSubst θ) ρ)
        (M.codeTerm (EXTRACT (EMB (applySubst θ r))))) := by sorry

end BergerSchwichtenberg1991

**`lemma_5`** — Given an admissible model $M : \mathrm{AdmissibleModel}$ in universe $u$, an inversion functional package $\mathrm{IF} : \mathrm{InversionFunctionals}(M)$ (providing $\Phi_\tau \in M^{\tau \to f}$ and $\Psi_\tau \in M^{f \to \tau}$ for each $\tau \in \mathrm{Ty}$), an implicit simple type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$, an implicit raw term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$, and a substitution $\theta : \mathrm{Var} \to \mathrm{Term}$ such that:
- $r$ has type $\rho$ ($\mathrm{HasType}(r, \rho)$),
- $r$ is in long $\beta$-normal form at type $\rho$ ($\mathrm{IsLongBetaNormal}(\rho, r)$), and
- $\theta$ is well-typed ($\mathrm{IsWellTypedSubst}(\theta)$, i.e., $\forall x \in \mathrm{Var},\; \mathrm{HasType}(\theta(x), x.\mathrm{ty})$),

the theorem asserts the conjunction of two claims, where $\eta_\theta \in M.\mathrm{Env}$ is the environment $y \mapsto \Psi_{y.\mathrm{ty}}(\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil \theta(y) \rceil^o)$ and $\mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, r)$ is the simultaneous capture-avoiding substitution of $\theta$ into $r$:
1. Applying $\Phi_\rho$ to the evaluation of $r$ in environment $\eta_\theta$ equals $\mathrm{emb}\ \lceil \mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, r) \rceil^o$ up to $=_f$:
   $$\Phi_\rho\bigl(M.\mathrm{eval}(r, \eta_\theta, \rho)\bigr) =_f \mathrm{emb}\ \lceil \mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, r) \rceil^o.$$
2. For every proof $\mathrm{hbase} : \rho = o$, transporting $M.\mathrm{eval}(r, \eta_\theta, \rho)$ along $\mathrm{hbase}$ to $M^o$ yields an element equal up to $=_o$ to the code of $\mathrm{EXTRACT}(\mathrm{EMB}(\mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, r)))$:
   $$\mathrm{hbase} \triangleright M.\mathrm{eval}(r, \eta_\theta, \rho) =_o \bigl\lceil \mathrm{EXTRACT}\bigl(\mathrm{EMB}(\mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, r))\bigr) \bigr\rceil^o.$$

items.milestone_description: Proves that `p-e_ρ` inverts evaluation and yields Strong Completeness in any admissible λ-model.
items.theorem_title: Theorem 1: Inversion of the Evaluation Functional in Admissible Models
items.formal_statement:
namespace BergerSchwichtenberg1991

universe u

theorem theorem_1 (M : AdmissibleModel.{u}) (IF : InversionFunctionals M) :
    (∀ (ρ : Ty) (a : M.Dom ρ),
      M.IsLambdaDefinable ρ a →
      ∃ t : Term,
        IF.IsPeResult ρ a t ∧
        IsClosed t ∧
        IsLongBetaNormal ρ t ∧
        ∀ η : M.Env, M.eqM ρ (M.eval t η ρ) a) ∧
    (∀ (ρ : Ty) (r rStar : Term) (θ : Substitution),
      HasType r ρ →
      HasType rStar ρ →
      IsLongBetaNormal ρ rStar →
      BetaEtaEq r rStar →
      IsWellTypedSubst θ →
      IF.IsPeResult ρ (M.eval r (IF.etaSubst θ) ρ) (EXTRACT (EMB (applySubst θ rStar))) ∧
      AlphaEq (EXTRACT (EMB (applySubst θ rStar))) (applySubst θ rStar)) ∧
    (∀ (ρ : Ty) (r s : Term),
      HasType r ρ →
      HasType s ρ →
      M.ModelsEq ρ r s →
      BetaEtaEq r s) := by sorry

end BergerSchwichtenberg1991
items.natural_language_statement: In any admissible model `M`, the procedure-to-expression functional `p-e_ρ` inverts evaluation on λ-definable elements and computes the long β-normal form of any closed term, yielding Strong Completeness (`M ⊨ r = s → r =_{βη} s`).
items.source: Ulrich Berger and Helmut Schwichtenberg, 'An inverse of the evaluation functional for typed λ-calculus', Proceedings of the Sixth Annual IEEE Symposium on Logic in Computer Science (LICS 1991), pp. 203-211 (doi:10.1109/LICS.1991.151645). Theorem 1 & Corollary, pp. 207-208.

**`theorem_1`** — Given an admissible model $M : \mathrm{AdmissibleModel}$ in universe $u$ and an inversion functional package $\mathrm{IF} : \mathrm{InversionFunctionals}(M)$, asserts the conjunction of three statements:
1. (**Inversion of $\lambda$-definable elements**) For every simple type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$ and every element $a \in M^\rho$ that is $\lambda$-definable in $M$ ($\mathrm{IsLambdaDefinable}(M, \rho, a)$, meaning there exists a closed term $r : \rho$ with $\forall \eta \in M.\mathrm{Env},\; M.\mathrm{eval}(r, \eta, \rho) =_\rho a$), there exists a term $t \in \mathrm{Term}$ such that:
   - $\mathrm{IF.IsPeResult}(\rho, a, t)$ holds (i.e., $\mathrm{HasType}(t, \rho)$ and $\lceil t \rceil^o =_o \mathrm{f\_extract}(\Phi_\rho\ a)$),
   - $t$ is closed ($\mathrm{IsClosed}(t)$, i.e., $\mathrm{freeVars}(t) = []$),
   - $t$ is in long $\beta$-normal form at type $\rho$ ($\mathrm{IsLongBetaNormal}(\rho, t)$), and
   - for every environment $\eta \in M.\mathrm{Env}$, $M.\mathrm{eval}(t, \eta, \rho) =_\rho a$.
2. (**Normalization under substitution**) For every simple type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$, all raw terms $r, r^* \in \mathrm{Term}$, and every substitution $\theta : \mathrm{Var} \to \mathrm{Term}$, if $r$ has type $\rho$ ($\mathrm{HasType}(r, \rho)$), $r^*$ has type $\rho$ ($\mathrm{HasType}(r^*, \rho)$), $r^*$ is in long $\beta$-normal form at type $\rho$ ($\mathrm{IsLongBetaNormal}(\rho, r^*)$), $r$ and $r^*$ are $\beta\eta$-equal ($\mathrm{BetaEtaEq}(r, r^*)$), and $\theta$ is well-typed ($\mathrm{IsWellTypedSubst}(\theta)$), then letting $t^* = \mathrm{EXTRACT}(\mathrm{EMB}(\mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, r^*)))$:
   - $\mathrm{IF.IsPeResult}\bigl(\rho,\, M.\mathrm{eval}(r, \eta_\theta, \rho),\, t^*\bigr)$ holds (i.e., $\mathrm{HasType}(t^*, \rho)$ and $\lceil t^* \rceil^o =_o \mathrm{f\_extract}\bigl(\Phi_\rho(M.\mathrm{eval}(r, \eta_\theta, \rho))\bigr)$), and
   - $t^*$ is $\alpha$-equivalent to $\mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, r^*)$ ($\mathrm{AlphaEq}(t^*, \mathrm{applySubst}(\theta, r^*))$).
3. (**Completeness**) For every simple type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$ and all raw terms $r, s \in \mathrm{Term}$, if $\mathrm{HasType}(r, \rho)$, $\mathrm{HasType}(s, \rho)$, and $M.\mathrm{ModelsEq}(\rho, r, s)$ (i.e., $\forall \eta \in M.\mathrm{Env},\; M.\mathrm{eval}(r, \eta, \rho) =_\rho M.\mathrm{eval}(s, \eta, \rho)$), then $r$ and $s$ are $\beta\eta$-equal ($\mathrm{BetaEtaEq}(r, s)$).

Note that Part 1 and Part 3 do not assume as a hypothesis that the witnessing closed term $r$ (in Part 1) or the terms $r, s$ (in Part 3) possess long $\beta$-normal forms $r^*$ satisfying $\mathrm{BetaEtaEq}(r, r^*)$, whereas Part 2 explicitly takes $r^*$ with $\mathrm{IsLongBetaNormal}(\rho, r^*)$ and $\mathrm{BetaEtaEq}(r, r^*)$ as inputs.

items.formal_statement:
namespace BergerSchwichtenberg1991

universe u

theorem completeness_pr_models :
    (∀ (M : PRModel.{u}) (N : EffectiveNumbering)
       (hExtractComb :
         ∀ indextBar : M.Dom (.arr .base (.arr .base .base)),
           ∃ extractBar : M.Dom (.arr (.arr .base .base) .base),
             ∀ a : M.Dom (.arr .base .base),
               M.eqM .base (M.appM extractBar a)
                 (M.appM a
                   (M.appM
                     (M.appM indextBar (M.appM a (M.nu (N.natOfIdx epsIdx))))
                     (M.appM a (M.nu (N.natOfIdx zeroIdx))))))
       (hStepComb :
         ∀ (abstBar : Ty → M.Dom (.arr .base (.arr .base .base)))
           (funBar appendBar : M.Dom (.arr .base (.arr .base .base)))
           (ρ : Ty) (body : M.Dom .base → M.Dom .base),
           (∀ p₁ p₂ : M.Dom .base, M.eqM .base p₁ p₂ → M.eqM .base (body p₁) (body p₂)) →
           ∃ step : M.Dom (.arr .base .base),
             ∀ p : M.Dom .base,
               M.eqM .base (M.appM step p)
                 (M.appM (M.appM (abstBar ρ) p)
                   (M.appM (M.appM funBar (body p))
                     (M.appM (M.appM appendBar p) (M.nu (N.natOfIdx zeroIdx))))))
       (hIF :
         ∀ A : AdmissibleModel.{u},
           A.toLambdaModel = M.toLambdaModel →
           Nonempty (InversionFunctionals A)),
      ∃ (A : AdmissibleModel.{u}) (IF : InversionFunctionals A),
        A.toLambdaModel = M.toLambdaModel ∧
        (∀ t : Term, HEq (A.codeTerm t) (M.nu (N.natOfTerm t))) ∧
        (∀ (ρ : Ty) (a : A.Dom ρ),
          A.IsLambdaDefinable ρ a →
          ∃ r : Term,
            HasType r ρ ∧
            IsClosed r ∧
            IsLongBetaNormal ρ r ∧
            A.eqM .base (IF.invCode ρ a) (A.codeTerm r) ∧
            ∀ η : A.Env, A.eqM ρ (A.eval r η ρ) a) ∧
        (∀ (ρ : Ty) (r s : Term),
          HasType r ρ →
          HasType s ρ →
          M.ModelsEq ρ r s →
          BetaEtaEq r s)) := by sorry

end BergerSchwichtenberg1991

**`completeness_pr_models`** — For every primitive recursive $\lambda$-model $M : \mathrm{PRModel}$ in universe $u$ and every effective numbering $N : \mathrm{EffectiveNumbering}$, given three combinator- and functional-existence hypotheses:
1. (`hExtractComb`) for every binary operation $\overline{\mathrm{indext}} \in M^{o \to o \to o}$, there exists $\overline{\mathrm{extract}} \in M^{(o \to o) \to o}$ such that for all $a \in M^{o \to o}$,
   $$\overline{\mathrm{extract}}\ a =_o a\ \Bigl(\overline{\mathrm{indext}}\ \bigl(a\ (\nu(\mathrm{natOfIdx}(\varepsilon)))\bigr)\ \bigl(a\ (\nu(\mathrm{natOfIdx}(0)))\bigr)\Bigr);$$
2. (`hStepComb`) for every type-indexed family $\overline{\mathrm{abst}} : \mathrm{Ty} \to M^{o \to o \to o}$, elements $\overline{\mathrm{fun}}, \overline{\mathrm{append}} \in M^{o \to o \to o}$, simple type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$, and meta-level function $\mathrm{body} : M^o \to M^o$ satisfying $\forall p_1, p_2 \in M^o,\; p_1 =_o p_2 \implies \mathrm{body}(p_1) =_o \mathrm{body}(p_2)$, there exists $\mathrm{step} \in M^{o \to o}$ such that for all $p \in M^o$,
   $$\mathrm{step}\ p =_o \overline{\mathrm{abst}}_\rho\ p\ \Bigl(\overline{\mathrm{fun}}\ (\mathrm{body}(p))\ \bigl(\overline{\mathrm{append}}\ p\ (\nu(\mathrm{natOfIdx}(0)))\bigr)\Bigr);$$
3. (`hIF`) for every admissible model $A : \mathrm{AdmissibleModel}$ in universe $u$ with $A.\mathrm{toLambdaModel} = M.\mathrm{toLambdaModel}$, the type $\mathrm{InversionFunctionals}(A)$ is nonempty;

the theorem asserts that there exist an admissible model $A : \mathrm{AdmissibleModel}$ in universe $u$ and an inversion functional package $\mathrm{IF} : \mathrm{InversionFunctionals}(A)$ such that:
- $A$'s underlying $\mathrm{LambdaModel}$ equals $M$'s underlying $\mathrm{LambdaModel}$ ($A.\mathrm{toLambdaModel} = M.\mathrm{toLambdaModel}$);
- for every raw term $t \in \mathrm{Term}$, $A.\mathrm{codeTerm}(t)$ is heterogeneously equal ($\mathrm{HEq}$) to $M.\nu(N.\mathrm{natOfTerm}(t))$;
- (**Inversion and normalization**) for every simple type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$ and every element $a \in A^\rho$ satisfying $\mathrm{IsLambdaDefinable}(A, \rho, a)$ (meaning there exists a closed term $t : \rho$ with $\forall \eta \in A.\mathrm{Env},\; A.\mathrm{eval}(t, \eta, \rho) =_\rho a$), there exists a term $r \in \mathrm{Term}$ such that $\mathrm{HasType}(r, \rho)$, $\mathrm{IsClosed}(r)$, $\mathrm{IsLongBetaNormal}(\rho, r)$, $\mathrm{IF.invCode}(\rho, a) =_o A.\mathrm{codeTerm}(r)$ in $A^o$, and $\forall \eta \in A.\mathrm{Env},\; A.\mathrm{eval}(r, \eta, \rho) =_\rho a$; and
- (**Completeness**) for every simple type $\rho \in \mathrm{Ty}$ and all raw terms $r, s \in \mathrm{Term}$, if $\mathrm{HasType}(r, \rho)$, $\mathrm{HasType}(s, \rho)$, and $M.\mathrm{ModelsEq}(\rho, r, s)$ (i.e., $\forall \eta \in M.\mathrm{Env},\; M.\mathrm{eval}(r, \eta, \rho) =_\rho M.\mathrm{eval}(s, \eta, \rho)$), then $\mathrm{BetaEtaEq}(r, s)$.
